subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during a single, continuous journey through the subterranean tunnels of Gracklstugh, beginning with the aftermath of a battle and ending at a cavern of ritual madness.
source_quote: And so we continue on our journey through the caves...

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: session date
fact: This event occurs during the session following the party’s descent into the lower tunnels of Gracklstugh, after the defeat of previous threats and before confronting larger factions. The timeline is marked by escalating tension and the revelation of hidden loyalties.
source_quote: Now let’s take a look at her more closely...

subject: session date
fact: This sequence occurs during the party’s continued journey through the Underdark, following the collapse of the Ashwood Council and the flight from surface civilization.
source_quote: And so we continue on our journey through the caves...

subject: the day the Ember Vanguard entered the ritual cavern
fact: On this day, the Ember Vanguard entered a cavern filled with Trillimac books, ritual circles, and Derro conducting experiments for Demogorgon, and killed Skiit, intimidated Ulnara, and narrowly avoided a patrol.
source_quote: I walk in quietly. We don’t need light, because we can all see in the dark... I finally spot the inhabitants, some Derro and Death dogs... Narrak... shouts - 'We are conducting experiments!'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz casts Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp to crush the Derro Skiit, who is beginning to wake up.
source_quote: I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp and start to crush the poor unfortunate creature.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz casts Toll the Dead, and the Derro Skiit’s heart stops and he dies.
source_quote: So I cast Toll the Dead, and the deadly chimes echo throughout the caves, but only it’s intended target hears them, and his heart stops, and he dies.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz enters a cavern with a hellish red glow, spiral patterns on the walls, and a glowing ritual circle on a platform.
source_quote: The cavern floor rises to form a natural 5-foot-high platform. A glowing ritual circle dominates the top of the platform.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz finds books titled “The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,” “The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn,” and “Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast,” confirming Demogorgon’s influence.
source_quote: I look carefully and notice a few of the titles - “The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,” and “The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn”, and “Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notes that the Derro are conducting experiments and chanting in unison under Narrak’s direction.
source_quote: They chant back at him - “For what purpose!”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices a Derro standing over a pit with an unbelievable smell emanating from it.
source_quote: I see a single Derro standing over a pit, with an unbelievable smell emanating from it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices the Derro is wearing an amulet of Demogorgon.
source_quote: Wait, that’s interesting, he’s got an amulet of Demogorgon.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observes that the Derro are terrified of Drow and react with subservience when confronted by their presence.
source_quote: Ulnara looks at me, and she realizes that I am Drow. And that the Drow do not mess around.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observes the Derro muttering to himself and recalls that such muttering is a common trait among the irrevocably insane of the Derro.
source_quote: Now that’s interesting, he seems to be muttering to himself. Bah, it’s a common trait among the irrevocably insane of the Derro.

subject: Daz kills Skiit with Toll the Dead
fact: Daz casts Toll the Dead, whose chimes are heard only by the target, causing Skiit’s heart to stop and killing him instantly, despite prior escape attempts.
source_quote: So I cast Toll the Dead, and the deadly chimes echo throughout the caves, but only it’s intended target hears them, and his heart stops, and he dies.

subject: Derro Attack After Bahamut Invocation
fact: Grygum’s declaration of faith in Bahamut triggered an immediate, violent attack from the Derro, who perceive it as blasphemy against their two-headed deity. The party was forced into combat despite attempts at diplomacy.
source_quote: The moment that Grygum mentioned 'Bahamut,' I knew we were in for it. These Derro... don't take kindly to anything outside their two-headed deity. And sure enough, they immediately attack.

subject: derro madness observation
fact: Zalthir observes the Derro’s madness and acts without speaking, knowing their nature.
source_quote: I observe everything and say nothing. My mind is clear. I act without speaking. I do because I know.

subject: derro patrol encounter
fact: A Derro patrol stumbles upon the Ember Vanguard and immediately attacks upon hearing the name 'Bahamut.'
source_quote: The moment that Grygum mentioned 'Bahamut,' I knew we were in for it. And sure enough, they immediately attack.

subject: Derro Patrol Encounter
fact: The party was ambushed by a Derro patrol after successfully bypassing their lair. Daz’s confidence in their stealth was proven correct as the Derro reacted with fear and derangement rather than aggression.
source_quote: And so we continue on our journey through the caves, when a Derro patrol stumbles on us. Daz insists we march as if we own this place. And it works. The creatures are fearful and somewhat deranged.

subject: Discovery of Demogorgon Ritual Evidence
fact: Daz uncovered a ritual chamber filled with texts and papers implicating Demogorgon in the Derro’s corruption. The evidence is sufficient to convince Errde Blackstaff, though Daz considers withholding it to prevent manipulation.
source_quote: Errde Blackstaff wants evidence of Demogorgon’s influence, and here it is. And amongst the books are various papers.

subject: Divine Scrutiny
fact: A term Grygum invents to avoid answering direct questions about his allegiance. It is a theatrical facade masking his uncertainty and hypocrisy, used to confuse and delay adversaries with pseudo-theological verbosity.
source_quote: ‘It is, in fact, a Divine Scrutiny, a profound act of investigation into the very threads of our intertwined fates...’

subject: divine scrutiny
fact: Grygum invokes a Divine Scrutiny, a profound act of investigation into the threads of intertwined fates in Gracklstugh.
source_quote: a Divine Scrutiny, a profound act of investigation into the very threads of our intertwined fates, here in this churning city of Gracklstugh

subject: emerald vanguard naming
fact: Grygum declares the group the 'Ember Guard,' later corrected to 'Ember Vanguard.'
source_quote: We are the Ember Guard," shouts Grygum. I smile. I like that name.

subject: experimental ritual
fact: An experimental ritual is being conducted by Narrak and his apprentices in service of Demogorgon’s will.
source_quote: We are conducting experiments!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum claims the question of allegiance is a Divine Scrutiny requiring consideration of Aspects of the Truth and Divine Ledgers.
source_quote: That is a question that requires more than a simple answer. It is, in fact, a Divine Scrutiny, a profound act of investigation into the very threads of our intertwined fates, here in this churning city of Gracklstugh.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum pretends to be a preacher and responds to Ulnara with his preacher’s voice to maintain control.
source_quote: “We shall, certainly,” says Grygum in his preacher’s voice.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum pushes the Derro over the cliff while Daz unleashes a light show.
source_quote: I push him over the cliff. At the same time, Daz unleashes a light show.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum shouts, 'May the power of the platinum dragon cure us all!' as a theatrical act of divine magic.
source_quote: “May the power of the platinum dragon cure us all!” I shout.

subject: Grygum pushes Skiit into the pit
fact: Grygum pushes Skiit over the cliff at the same time Daz unleashes a light show, triggering a chain of events that leads to Skiit's resurrection and eventual death by Toll the Dead.
source_quote: I push him over the cliff. At the same time, Daz unleashes a light show.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak shouts, 'We are conducting experiments! For the elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!'
source_quote: He shouts - “We are conducting experiments!” They chant back at him - “For what purpose!” He screams - “The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!”

subject: Narrak conducts ritual experiments
fact: Narrak leads Derro apprentices in ritual experiments under the red glow of the cavern, chanting to elevate the Derro, triumph Demogorgon, and destroy the Duergar, surrounded by forbidden texts.
source_quote: We are conducting experiments! For what purpose! The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: narrak's experiment
fact: Narrak, a Derro with warped intellect, leads experiments for the elevation of the Derro and the triumph of Demogorgon.
source_quote: We are conducting experiments! ... The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: pit trap discovery
fact: A poorly disguised pit trap is discovered upon entering the hellish cavern.
source_quote: I look down at what he is pointing at, and it’s a poorly disguised pit trap.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin declares 'East' when asked whether to go left or right, ending the discussion.
source_quote: I say - “East.”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin dismisses two mad Derro as having no value and chooses not to fight them.
source_quote: I squint at the tents and the room and say, “No. There is nothing of value here.”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin kills a Derro with his longsword and declares, 'This is how the Bahamut walks!'
source_quote: I brought my longsword down hard on the Derro, attacking Grygum. The sword cut through his flimsy armor and into his chest, and it dropped like a sack of rocks. Dead. "This is how the Bahamut walks!" I declared, standing over his fallen form, ready to take on the next fool who dared challenge us.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin observes that the Derro are Dwarves corrupted by mindflayers, barely Dwarves anymore, and not creatures to reason with.
source_quote: The Derro themselves were predictably clumsy. One swung at me, but my armor held. The other landed a hit on Grygum, but our allies were quick to retaliate, dealing a good chunk of damage to him. Zalthir, bless his arcane heart, summoned his darkness, enveloping a couple of them. Then, in a burst of brilliant speed, he critically struck one of the Darrow. Impressive. Daz, always quick with a spell, launched his magic missiles. A flurry of arcane energy streaked across the tunnel, and the Derro had struck, already reeling, and fell. One down. Good. The remaining Derro, true to their limited intellect, continued their mindless attacks. One swung wildly at Zalthir, missing entirely. Another charged Grygum, screaming some incoherent babble about their master. My armor held, and I parried his pathetic attack. "One head is better than two!" I roared, pushing him back. My chance came again, and I didn't hesitate. I brought my longsword down hard on the Derro, attacking Grygum. The sword cut through his flimsy armor and into his chest, and it dropped like a sack of rocks. Dead. "This is how the Bahamut walks!" I declared, standing over his fallen form, ready to take on the next fool who dared challenge us. But they were all dead.

subject: Thorin declares 'East' at the fork
fact: Thorin, exhausted by debate, arbitrarily declares 'East' as the path forward, leading the group toward a chamber filled with cages, Derro muttering about the prince’s hunger and dark lake scales.
source_quote: Left or right?' I ask. The discussion begins, and I am too tired for this, so I say - 'East.'

subject: toll the dead casting
fact: Daz casts Toll the Dead, its chimes echoing only for the intended target, killing the Derro instantly.
source_quote: I cast Toll the Dead, and the deadly chimes echo throughout the caves, but only it’s intended target hears them, and his heart stops, and he dies.

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: zombie creation
fact: Ulnara promises to turn Skiit into a zombie to serve the cult of Demogorgon forever.
source_quote: after he’s dead I will turn him into a zombie and he will serve the cult of Demogorgon forever!

subject: Cult of Demogorgon
fact: A dangerous and chaotic cult that has infiltrated derro society, promising power and restoration to the broken. Skiit and Ulnara are true believers, interpreting Demogorgon’s influence as divine mandate. Their devotion warps their perception of reality and loyalty.
source_quote: I am a follower of Demogorgon! Pliinki has said that anybody who follows Demogorgon is making the Derro proud and powerful.

subject: Cult of Demogorgon
fact: A pervasive, decentralized cult among the Derro that worships the Two-Headed Demon Lord as the source of their twisted power and supposed redemption. It is used to justify atrocities, control lower Derro, and oppose the Duergar. Its influence is evident in rituals, tomes, and the delusions of its followers.
source_quote: ‘The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!’

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are a collective faction devoted to the elevation of their kind and the triumph of Demogorgon, with a genocidal intent toward the Duergar.
source_quote: The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are a race of mad, twisted dwarves once enslaved and mentally corrupted by mind flayers. They are obsessed with Demogorgon, prone to delusions of grandeur, and incapable of rational diplomacy. Their society is fragmented, chaotic, and dominated by cultish fervor.
source_quote: They are Dwarves that were slaves of the mindflayers, who corrupted their fundamental nature until they are barely Dwarves. They are mad.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are a subterranean race of twisted, insane dwarves once enslaved by mind flayers. Their minds were shattered, leaving them paranoid, superstitious, and obsessed with false gods like Demogorgon. They serve as necromancers and laborers in the pits of Gracklstugh, perpetuating their broken culture.
source_quote: I recall the stories of the Derro, creatures that served the mind flayers and had their minds destroyed.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are former slaves of the mind flayers, whose minds were destroyed and replaced with fanatical devotion to Demogorgon, making them mad, paranoid, and incapable of rational discourse with outsiders.
source_quote: The Derro are Dwarves that were slaves of the mindflayers, who corrupted their fundamental nature until they are barely Dwarves. They are mad. These are not creatures to reason with.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are a subterranean dwarven race hostile to the Derro, often seen as oppressors or rivals. The Derro cultists blame them for their suffering and vow destruction, though the Duergar themselves are not present in this scene.
source_quote: ‘I don’t believe you guys work for us. I think you work for the Duergar or the Mindflayers!’

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are a targeted faction of the Derro, subject to their genocidal campaign in service of Demogorgon’s triumph.
source_quote: The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a disciplined group of explorers and spellcasters who operate with stealth and tactical precision. They enter dangerous caverns without light, isolate themselves from non-combatants, and prioritize evidence collection over direct confrontation.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard will march in, but we tell our companions to wait outside.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a group that claims authority over the caverns, uses intimidating titles, and manipulates Derro through fear and psychological dominance, though their true allegiance is ambiguous.
source_quote: We are the Ember Guard," shouts Grygum. I smile. I like that name.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a name invented by Grygum to intimidate and unify the party’s identity. It is not a real organization but a performative label used to project authority over derro and cultists. Ulnara adopts it to appease the Drow, believing it to be a powerful faction.
source_quote: We are the Ember Guard," shouts Grygum. I smile. I like that name.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a self-proclaimed group that Grygum and Daz adopt as a cover identity to intimidate derro and other cave-dwellers. It is a fabricated title with no formal structure, used strategically to project authority and exploit fear of the unknown.
source_quote: ‘We are the Ember Guard,’ shouts Grygum. I smile. I like that name.

subject: cage chamber
fact: Cages assembled from scrap iron line both sides of a chamber, with a spiral path marked by stone pylons.
source_quote: cages assembled from scrap iron on both sides of the chamber. A spiral path circles into the center of the room, marked off by small stone pylons.

subject: cave entrance with brimstone stench
fact: A cave entrance emits a stench of brimstone and chemicals, distinct from the usual Derro decay.
source_quote: the unspeakable stench that seems to follow the Derro emanates here. This time it is the smell of brimstone and chemicals.

subject: cave entrance with fungi and offal
fact: A cavern entrance features mounds of fungi and offal flanking a narrow tunnel.
source_quote: a crack in the southeast wall of the pit leads to a narrow tunnel, flanked by mounds of fungi and offal.

subject: Derro Chamber with Scrap-Iron Cages
fact: This cavern is filled with scrap-iron cages, spiral stone pylons, and bubbling cauldrons emitting a foul odor. It is the lair of deranged Derro who worship a two-headed deity and perform forbidden rituals. The air is thick with the stench of decay and magical corruption.
source_quote: The smell is coming from cages assembled from scrap iron on both sides of the chamber. A spiral path circles into the center of the room, marked off by small stone pylons.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: A churning, subterranean city of madness and decay, where derro, duergar, and mind flayers clash in secret wars. The pit of Ulnara is one of many necromantic operations hidden in its tunnels, sustained by fear, faith, and the lingering influence of ancient enslavement.
source_quote: Here in this churning city of Gracklstugh.

subject: gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is the churning city where Divine Scrutiny and tangled fates occur.
source_quote: here in this churning city of Gracklstugh

subject: pit of Ulnara
fact: The pit of Ulnara contains body parts and zombies, fed by the Derro for the great project.
source_quote: tossing body parts over the ledge into the pit

subject: ritual cavern
fact: The ritual cavern is lit by hellish red glow, with spiral patterns on walls, silent dripping water, and rampantly growing fungi; it contains books titled 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn,' and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'
source_quote: The cavern floor rises to form a natural 5-foot-high platform. A glowing ritual circle dominates the top of the platform. Around the platform are books made from Trillimac... 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' and 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn', and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'

subject: Ritual Cavern of the Two-Headed Beast
fact: A vast subterranean cavern lit by hellish red glow, with spiraling wall patterns, silent dripping water, and rampant fungal growth. At its center lies a glowing ritual circle, surrounded by forbidden tomes on duality, madness, and spawn creation, indicating deep Demogorgon influence.
source_quote: The cavern floor rises to form a natural 5-foot-high platform. A glowing ritual circle dominates the top of the platform. Around the platform are books made from Trillimac.

subject: ritual platform
fact: A glowing ritual circle dominates a 5-foot-high natural platform in the cavern.
source_quote: The cavern floor rises to form a natural 5-foot-high platform. A glowing ritual circle dominates the top of the platform.

subject: the chamber of experiments
fact: The chamber is a deeply unsettling space where Narrak and his apprentices conduct experiments under the influence of Demogorgon.
source_quote: His presence in this space is deeply unsettling, a chilling testament to the insidious influence of the demon lord he serves.

subject: The Pit of Ulnara
fact: A vast, stinking chasm in the southeast wall of the tunnel, filled with decomposing flesh, offal, fungi, and shambling zombies. It is the heart of the Derro necromantic project, fed by body parts tossed over the edge. The faerzress glows around it like fog, concealing the true horror within.
source_quote: The glow of faerzress is everywhere, seeming to flow like fog around dark shapes shambling across the pit.

subject: tunnel turn
fact: The tunnel turn leads to the pit where the Derro stands over body parts.
source_quote: I follow Grygum and Thorin around the turn of the tunnel and see a single Derro standing over a pit

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Death Dogs
fact: Canine undead creatures that patrol the cavern with Narrak’s ritual circle. They are likely bred or raised by the Derro cultists as guardians and are attuned to the foul energies of the space.
source_quote: The cavern floor rises... and I finally spot the inhabitants, some Derro and Death dogs.

subject: Death dogs
fact: Death dogs are predatory, supernatural canines that accompany Derro in their subterranean lairs. They are silent, stealthy, and blend into the hellish red glow of the caverns, remaining unnoticed until provoked.
source_quote: I finally spot the inhabitants, some Derro and Death dogs. They don’t notice us, so we continue.

subject: Death dogs
fact: Death dogs are present in the ritual cavern alongside Derro, silently observing the rituals without initiating conflict until provoked.
source_quote: And I finally spot the inhabitants, some Derro and Death dogs. They don’t notice us, so we continue.

subject: Demogorgon
fact: Demogorgon is a demon lord being served by Narrak and the Derro, whose influence drives their chaotic evil and genocidal agenda.
source_quote: The Triumph of Demogorgon

subject: derro count
fact: A single Derro stands over a pit with an unbelievable smell emanating from it.
source_quote: a single Derro standing over a pit, with an unbelievable smell emanating from it

subject: derro cultists
fact: Two Derro speak incoherently near a tent, one obsessed with the prince’s hunger, the other with the dark lake and obsidian scales.
source_quote: More of this, always more, the mastery demands... Water it chips, not like the dark lake. There, I pulled something from the dark ones, A scale smooth, this polished obsidian, but it shimmered like madness.

subject: derro named skiit
fact: Skiit, a Derro, is tossed into the pit by Grygum, later awakens, and seeks permission to kill Spiderbait.
source_quote: Skiit looks at me and then points at Spiderbait, 'Can I kill that one over there?'

subject: Derro patrol
fact: A Derro patrol stumbles upon the Ember Vanguard, immediately attacking upon hearing the name Bahamut, revealing their fanatical devotion to Demogorgon and hatred of outsider deities.
source_quote: The moment that Grygum mentioned 'Bahamut,' I knew we were in for it. These Derro... don't take kindly to anything outside their two-headed deity. And sure enough, they immediately attack.

subject: derro patrol members
fact: Multiple Derro, corrupted former dwarves of the mind flayers, attack the Ember Vanguard after hearing Bahamut’s name.
source_quote: The Derro themselves were predictably clumsy... They are mad. These are not creatures to reason with.

subject: narrak
fact: Narrak, a Derro with frenetic, terrifying intellect, leads ritual experiments for Demogorgon’s triumph.
source_quote: Narrak. His pale, derro features are perpetually contorted, twisting into a grotesque mask of terrifying, spiraling madness.

subject: Ogre Zombie
fact: An Ogre Zombie emerges from a crack in the southeast wall of the pit, demanding to know who intrudes, and is confronted by the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: From there, a voice and an Ogre Zombie emerge. 'What is the meaning of this? Who are you? Who do you think you are?'

subject: ogre zombie
fact: An Ogre Zombie emerges from a crack in the southeast wall of the pit.
source_quote: a voice and an Ogre Zombie emerge.

subject: Ogre Zombie
fact: An Ogre Zombie emerges from the pit, demanding answers from the party. It is part of Ulnara’s undead workforce, shambling among offal and fungi, and is likely a failed experiment or reanimated guard from the derro project.
source_quote: What is the meaning of this? Who are you? Who do you think you are?

subject: Ogre Zombie
fact: An undead brute that emerges from the pit, demanding answers. It is part of Ulnara’s undead army and exhibits the mindless aggression typical of reanimated giants, though its speech suggests lingering sentience or necromantic corruption.
source_quote: ‘What is the meaning of this? Who are you? Who do you think you are?’

subject: Zombies
fact: Numerous zombies fill the pit below Ulnara’s operation, constructed from body parts tossed over the ledge. They are the living result of the Derro’s necromantic project, animated and controlled by Ulnara for the cult of Demogorgon.
source_quote: I see a lot of zombies.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a Drow wizard and lethal pragmatist who uses precision magic to eliminate threats. He kills Skiit with Toll the Dead, crushes undead with Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp, and breaks Ulnara’s arrogance by revealing his race. He prefers direct action over rhetoric and is unimpressed by cultist posturing.
source_quote: I snap my fingers, trying to kill him, but the derro escapes. So I cast Toll the Dead...

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a quick-witted spellcaster who specializes in magic missiles and tactical leadership. He commands the Ember Vanguard, insists on caution, and is the first to recognize ritualistic evidence of Demogorgon’s influence in the caves.
source_quote: Daz, always quick with a spell, launched his magic missiles. A flurry of arcane energy streaked across the tunnel, and the Derro had struck, already reeling, and fell.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a ruthless, calculating Drow spellcaster who operates with cold efficiency. He uses fear, lethal magic, and precise strikes to dominate derro and necromancers. He is pragmatic, distrustful of evidence, and sees through the delusions of others.
source_quote: ‘I snap my fingers... but the derro escapes.’ ‘Toll the Dead... his heart stops, and he dies.’

subject: Derro
fact: Derro are corrupted former dwarven slaves of mindflayers, now mad and devoted to a two-headed deity. They are physically weak, intellectually limited, and violently hostile to outsiders—especially those who invoke Bahamut. They inhabit caverns lined with scrap-iron cages and ritual cauldrons.
source_quote: The Derro themselves were predictably clumsy... They are mad. These are not creatures to reason with.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are described as slaves of the mindflayers, whose fundamental nature was corrupted until they are barely Dwarves and are mad.
source_quote: The Derro themselves were predictably clumsy. One swung at me, but my armor held. The other landed a hit on Grygum, but our allies were quick to retaliate, dealing a good chunk of damage to him. Zalthir, bless his arcane heart, summoned his darkness, enveloping a couple of them. Then, in a burst of brilliant speed, he critically struck one of the Darrow. Impressive. Daz, always quick with a spell, launched his magic missiles. A flurry of arcane energy streaked across the tunnel, and the Derro had struck, already reeling, and fell. One down. Good. The remaining Derro, true to their limited intellect, continued their mindless attacks. One swung wildly at Zalthir, missing entirely. Another charged Grygum, screaming some incoherent babble about their master. My armor held, and I parried his pathetic attack. "One head is better than two!" I roared, pushing him back. subject: Derro
fact: The Derro believes he is a true believer of Demogorgon and that following Demogorgon makes the Derro proud and powerful.
source_quote: I am a follower of Demogorgon! Pliinki has said that anybody who follows Demogorgon is making the Derro proud and powerful. And we’re going to be great again!

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro has blue-gray skin, pale eyes lacking irises and pupils, and thin, stringy hair that is dull white and constantly greasy.
source_quote: He has blue, gray skin and pale eyes that lack both irises and pupils. He has thin, stringy hair, dull white, constantly looking greasy and unkempt.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro revere a two-headed deity and are hostile to any outside religious claims, especially Bahamut.
source_quote: These Derro, bless their simple, deranged minds, don't take kindly to anything outside their two-headed deity.

subject: Derro
fact: Two Derro in the chamber speak incoherently, one about the prince’s hunger and the other about pulling a scale from the dark lake that shimmered like madness.
source_quote: More of this, always mor,e the mastery demands. Many contributions, the prince is hungry, always hungry,” says one. The other intones as it stares intently into the murky bubbling cauldron, tracing an invisible pattern with a dirty finger, “Water it chips, not like the dark lake. There, I pulled something from the dark ones, A scale smooth, this polished obsidian, but it shimmered like madness. In the dim light came from the deep, the deepest part with voices seeing.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes Bahamut is boring and Stroud was exciting.
source_quote: Bahamut is boring. Stroud was exciting. Bahamut, not so much.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a charismatic, preacher-like cleric who claims to worship Bahamut but uses theatricality and psychological manipulation to control derro. He is emotionally inconsistent, alternating between gentleness and cruelty, and often misjudges derro reactions due to his temple-bred naivete.
source_quote: ‘I worship Bahamut!’ ‘That is a question that requires more than a simple answer. It is, in fact, a Divine Scrutiny...’

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of Bahamut who uses theatrical divine rhetoric to mask his own uncertainty. He pushed Skiit into the pit, interrogated Ulnara about the project’s progress, and coined the name 'Ember Guard' to intimidate. His gentleness fails to control derro, but his bluster and actions create openings for Daz.
source_quote: That is a question that requires more than a simple answer. It is, in fact, a Divine Scrutiny...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of Bahamut who uses theatricality and performative piety to manipulate others.
source_quote: “I worship Bahamut!”

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a preacher who proclaims, 'I worship Bahamut!' and is met with immediate hostility from Derro who revere Demogorgon as their sole deity.
source_quote: I worship Bahamut!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a preacher who worships Bahamut and is prone to shouting philosophical declarations in dangerous situations. He is currently leading the party through Derro-infested caves and has provoked an attack by invoking Bahamut's name.
source_quote: I worship Bahamut!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum mutters that the two Derro are mad.
source_quote: Grygum mutters, “They are mad.”

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is a Derro ritualist with perpetually contorted features, frenetic eyes, and a warped intellect, leading experiments to elevate the Derro, triumph Demogorgon, and destroy the Duergar.
source_quote: We are conducting experiments! For what purpose! The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is a Derro with perpetually contorted features, unnervingly bright eyes, and a warped intellect consumed by chaotic evil, serving Demogorgon.
source_quote: His pale, derro features are perpetually contorted, twisting into a grotesque mask of terrifying, spiraling madness. His eyes, perhaps unnervingly bright in the dim light, dart about with a frenetic, almost desperate energy. He gestures wildly at a few apprentices. There’s an undeniable, warped intellect simmering beneath his frantic movements, but it is utterly consumed by the chaotic evil that seems to radiate from his very being.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is a derro orchestrator whose pale, contorted features radiate spiraling madness, serving the demon lord Demogorgon and consumed by chaotic evil.
source_quote: His eyes dart about with a frenetic, almost desperate energy.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is a derro ritualist and mad scholar who leads experiments in a cavern filled with Demogorgon-themed tomes. He is a terrifying blend of warped intellect and chaotic evil, obsessed with elevating the Derro, destroying the Duergar, and serving Demogorgon.
source_quote: ‘We are conducting experiments!... The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!’

subject: Skiit
fact: Skiit is a Derro who mutters to himself, wears tattered leather stained with grime, and carries an amulet of Demogorgon, believing that following the demon lord makes the Derro proud and powerful.
source_quote: I am a follower of Demogorgon! Pliinki has said that anybody who follows Demogorgon is making the Derro proud and powerful. And we're going to be great again!

subject: Skiit
fact: Skiit is a derro cultist of Demogorgon who believes following the demon lord will restore Derro pride and power. He is mentally unstable, mutters to himself, and obsesses over Pliinki’s promises. He was thrown into a pit by Grygum and later killed by Daz’s Toll the Dead.
source_quote: ‘Pliinki promised Skiit a better job.’ ‘I am a follower of Demogorgon! We’re going to be great again!’

subject: Skiit
fact: Skiit is a derro cultist of Demogorgon, mentally fractured and obsessed with promises of better jobs from Pliinki. He mutters to himself, wears tattered stained leather and cloth, and tends to a pit of body parts. He was pushed into the pit by Grygum, revived, and then killed by Daz with Toll the Dead.
source_quote: But Pliinki promised Skiit a better job.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a battle-hardened dwarf warrior who relies on brute force, armor, and blunt pragmatism. He dismisses madness as irrelevant, avoids unnecessary conflict, and has zero patience for philosophical talk. He is the group’s most effective combatant against derro.
source_quote: ‘One head is better than two!’ ‘No. There is nothing of value here.’ ‘East.’

subject: Ulnara
fact: Ulnara is a Derro necromancer and cultist of Demogorgon who transforms from arrogance to subservience upon realizing Daz is a Drow, and promises to turn corpses into zombies for the cult.
source_quote: Your lordship! Or was it the Ember Vanguard? What a wonderful name for such a powerful group. Do not worry, after he’s dead I will turn him into a zombie and he will serve the cult of Demogorgon forever!

subject: Ulnara
fact: Ulnara is a derro necromancer and cultist of Demogorgon who oversees the ‘great project of Ulnara of the Council of Savants.’ She initially appears arrogant but collapses into subservience upon realizing Daz is a Drow. She seeks to turn corpses into zombies for Demogorgon’s cult.
source_quote: ‘Your lordship! Or was it the Ember Vanguard?... I will turn him into a zombie and he will serve the cult of Demogorgon forever!’

subject: Ulnara
fact: Ulnara is a derro necromancer and high cultist of Demogorgon, in charge of the great project of Ulnara of the Council of Savants. She oversees the pit of zombies and body parts, initially arrogant but broken by Daz’s display of power after realizing he is a Drow. She offers service to the Ember Vanguard to save herself.
source_quote: The great project of Ulnara of the Council of Savants!

subject: Ulnara
fact: Ulnara is a necromancer, a cultist of Demogorgon, and a derro who shifts from arrogance to subservience upon realizing Daz is a Drow.
source_quote: Ulnara looks at me, and she has that look of someone who thought they had all the cards, and understood what was going on, and realizes she doesn’t anymore. Her arrogance disappears, and her sniveling, subservient persona emerges.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a silent, disciplined monk whose actions are precise and purposeful. He communicates only through deeds — summoning darkness, landing critical strikes, and observing without judgment. He is the group’s most reliable and composed member.
source_quote: I observe everything and say nothing. My mind is clear. I act without speaking. I do because I know.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an arcane spellcaster who uses darkness and critical strikes to devastating effect. He is exhausted but effective in combat, having critically struck a Derro with a precise spell and summoned darkness to envelop multiple enemies.
source_quote: Zalthir, bless his arcane heart, summoned his darkness, enveloping a couple of them. Then, in a burst of brilliant speed, he critically struck one of the Darrow.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observes everything and acts without speaking, driven by clear, unspoken knowledge.
source_quote: I observe everything and say nothing. My mind is clear. I act without speaking. I do because I know.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observes everything and says nothing, acting without speaking because he knows.
source_quote: I observe everything and say nothing. My mind is clear. I act without speaking. I do because I know.

subject: Amulet of Demogorgon
fact: A dark artifact worn by Skiit, symbolizing his allegiance to the Two-Headed Demon Lord. It is the key to his delusional belief in Derro supremacy and the source of his defiance against the party.
source_quote: Wait, that’s interesting, he’s got an amulet of Demogorgon.

subject: Amulet of Demogorgon
fact: A dark, twisted artifact worn by Skiit, radiating chaotic power and reinforcing his delusions of divine favor. It is the physical symbol of his allegiance to Demogorgon and the catalyst for his defiance against the party.
source_quote: Wait, that’s interesting, he’s got an amulet of Demogorgon.

subject: amulet of Demogorgon
fact: An amulet of Demogorgon is worn by Skiit, a Derro who believes it grants him divine favor and power, and is the sole symbol of his devotion in a world of fractured faith.
source_quote: Wait, that’s interesting, he’s got an amulet of Demogorgon.

subject: amulet of Demogorgon
fact: The Derro wears an amulet of Demogorgon.
source_quote: he’s got an amulet of Demogorgon

subject: death dogs
fact: Death dogs are present in the hellish red-glowing cavern with Derro.
source_quote: some Derro and Death dogs.

subject: demogorgon cultist derro
fact: The Derro named Skiit claims to be a follower of Demogorgon, believing it makes the Derro proud and powerful.
source_quote: I am a follower of Demogorgon! Pliinki has said that anybody who follows Demogorgon is making the Derro proud and powerful.

subject: derro hair and skin
fact: The Derro has blue-gray skin, pale eyes lacking irises and pupils, and dull white, greasy, unkempt hair.
source_quote: He has blue, gray skin and pale eyes that lack both irises and pupils. He has thin, stringy hair, dull white, constantly looking greasy and unkempt.

subject: derro papers
fact: Papers found among the Trillimac books contain evidence of Demogorgon’s influence.
source_quote: amongst the books are various papers. Knowing these creatures, there is probably enough evidence to convince Errde of whatever she wants.

subject: maximillian’s earthen grasp
fact: Daz uses Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp to crush the wounded Derro, but it escapes.
source_quote: I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp and start to crush the poor unfortunate creature.

subject: Polished Obsidian Scale
fact: A smooth, shimmering scale of polished obsidian, taken from the 'dark ones' by a Derro. It glows faintly in dim light and is described as shimmering 'like madness,' indicating magical corruption from the Deep Dark or Demogorgon's influence.
source_quote: A scale smooth, this polished obsidian, but it shimmered like madness.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: Trillimac books
fact: Books titled 'The Spiraling Descent,' 'The Prince's Gift,' and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast' are found in the ritual chamber.
source_quote: books made from Trillimac... 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn', 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'

subject: Trillimac Books
fact: These forbidden books, bound in Trillimac, contain esoteric rituals and theological treatises on the Two-Headed Beast, duality, and the creation of favored spawn. Titles include 'The Spiraling Descent,' 'The Prince's Gift,' and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.' They are key evidence of Demogorgon's corruption.
source_quote: Titles — 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' and 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn', and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'

subject: Trillimac books
fact: Trillimac books are found in the ritual cavern, inscribed with forbidden texts on duality, madness, and the creation of favored spawn for Demogorgon.
source_quote: Around the platform are books made from Trillimac... 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' and 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn', and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'

subject: Trillimac Tomes
fact: Books bound in Trillimac leather containing forbidden knowledge on Demogorgon’s influence, Derro ascension, and ritual madness. They are evidence of the cult’s scholarly corruption and serve as potential leverage against Errde Blackstaff.
source_quote: ‘The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,’ ‘The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn,’ ‘Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.’

subject: Daz's allegiance
fact: Daz is unsure who he and the Ember Vanguard work for, having struck numerous deals with various parties.
source_quote: However, we have struck numerous deals with various other parties, and I'm no longer sure what to say.

subject: Derro Ritual Texts and Their Origin
fact: The origin of the Trillimac books and the true identity of 'the Prince' referenced in the texts remain unknown. Whether 'the Prince' is Demogorgon, a mindflayer overlord, or something older is unconfirmed.
source_quote: The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn

subject: Divine Scrutiny
fact: Grygum frames questions of allegiance as 'Divine Scrutiny,' a profound act of investigation into the threads of intertwined fates, turning simple queries into meandering theological debates.
source_quote: That is a question that requires more than a simple answer. It is, in fact, a Divine Scrutiny, a profound act of investigation into the very threads of our intertwined fates, here in this churning city of Gracklstugh.

subject: Divine Scrutiny
fact: Grygum’s obsession with framing every question as a 'Divine Scrutiny' is a narrative thread that masks his own lack of certainty. It is a performative ritual he uses to avoid direct answers, but it inadvertently creates space for Daz’s lethal clarity to dominate.
source_quote: It is, in fact, a Divine Scrutiny, a profound act of investigation into the very threads of our intertwined fates...

subject: Grygum’s Faith and Its Consequences
fact: Grygum’s unyielding devotion to Bahamut repeatedly provokes deadly reactions from cultists. Whether this is divine courage or reckless folly remains in question, and future encounters may escalate beyond combat.
source_quote: Grygum shouts, 'I thought we could have a deep Phylosophical conversation!'

subject: Grygum's worship of Bahamut
fact: Grygum claims to worship Bahamut, but the Derro react violently to this, suggesting his faith is either performative or dangerously out of step with the local reality.
source_quote: “I worship Bahamut!”

subject: purpose of experiments
fact: The ultimate purpose of the experiments remains unresolved, tied to the Derro’s quest for elevation and Demogorgon’s triumph.
source_quote: For what purpose!

subject: The Fate of the Books
fact: Daz possesses the evidence but is undecided whether to deliver it to Errde Blackstaff. The moral and political consequences of revealing—or concealing—this knowledge are unresolved.
source_quote: I might not want to give it to her. But I know her type; if she doesn’t get evidence, she’ll invent it.

subject: The Great Project of Ulnara
fact: A mysterious, ongoing Derro necromantic operation overseen by Ulnara, involving body parts, zombies, and ritual sacrifice. Its true purpose is unknown, but it is tied to Demogorgon’s influence and the Derro’s desire for rebirth.
source_quote: ‘The great project of Ulnara of the Council of Savants!’
